doc.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Learning Kenton's style by playing Mulligan's charts
summary: Playing Mulligan's charts nightly in 1952 taught him what worked with Kenton.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Can you put into words what it was that after the nine months with Kenton, made you feel okay, now I feel I can start to write for this band? What did you need to do to match his style?

Well, the thing that helped me the most was playing Gerry Mulligan. He wrote about ten charts for Kenton when I joined the band in ’52, and playing those things every night was the big impetus. Because that was the first big time arrangements that I’d played. Well of course, Barnet, but I mean guys with my generation. You know Mulligan was the first guy that I got a chance to play and that was a great education. Because I could see how the things went over with Stan. Stan didn’t really like a lot of them, but he liked “Youngblood” and a few others. And so in assessing what I’m going to do for Stan, I was able to see his reaction to these other things, and kind of figure well don’t do that, whatever you do. Maybe this you could do.
At least your chances are improving, that it won’t get the ax.
